# NVIDIA B300 Price in 2026: Blackwell Ultra Specs, Hourly Rates and Reservations

The NVIDIA B300 pairs 288 GB of HBM3e with 1.5 times the B200's FP4 compute. This guide covers its specs, how B300 time is priced, fal's published B300 rates with worked cost examples, and how to reserve capacity.

Alex Matthews· Updated Oct 26, 2026· 7 min read

The NVIDIA B300 adds 50% more memory (288 GB) and 1.5 times the B200's dense FP4 compute at the same 8 TB/s, so it pays off for large, long-context or FP4-ready models. Bandwidth-bound models that fit in 192 GB cost less on a B200. On fal the B300 lists at $12.99 per GPU-hour, and as low as $5.99.

The B300, NVIDIA's Blackwell Ultra GPU, shows where inference hardware is heading: more memory per GPU and more compute at 4-bit precision, with no gain at the FP8 and FP16 precisions most models still run at. That makes it a specialist's GPU. For long-context reasoning and very large models, it can be the cheapest way to serve. For most other work, a B200 does the same job for less.

## What changed from the B200

- Memory. 288 GB of HBM3e per GPU, 50% more than the B200's 192 GB, at the same 8 TB/s. 1 
- FP4 compute. 15 petaFLOPS of dense NVFP4 per chip, against 10 for Blackwell. In 8-GPU HGX servers that is 13.5 against 9 per GPU. 1 2 
- Attention. NVIDIA rates attention-layer compute at up to 2 times Blackwell. 1 
- Networking. Each GPU in a DGX B300 gets an 800 Gb/s ConnectX-8 port, twice the 400 Gb/s in a DGX B200. 3 4 

FP8 and FP16 throughput did not change. FP64 and INT8 throughput fell sharply. 2

### Worked B300 cost examples

| Workload | Billed GPU time | List price ($12.99/h) | "As low as" ($5.99/h) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 hour on 8 GPUs | 8 GPU-hours | $103.92 | $47.92 |
| 1 GPU kept warm for a 30-day month | 720 GPU-hours | $9,352.80 | $4,312.80 |
| Bursty traffic: 3 runner-hours a day, 30 days | 90 GPU-hours | $1,169.10 | $539.10 |

The bursty month uses one-eighth of the warm month's GPU time, so it costs one-eighth as much. On a GPU this expensive, scaling to zero between bursts matters as much as the hourly rate, at the cost of cold starts when traffic returns.

## Buy or rent a B300

B300s are sold mainly inside 8-GPU servers, priced per deal. To compare a quote, renting one GPU for a year (8,760 hours) costs:

- $113,792.40 at list price.
- $52,472.40 at the "as low as" rate.

A purchase adds power, liquid cooling, networking, space and staff, and costs the same whether busy or idle. An 8-GPU DGX B300 draws about 14 kW. 3 Owning makes sense mainly if you already run large data centers and can keep B300s busy around the clock.

### Hourly (on-demand) rates

The headline number is an hourly price per GPU. Two questions decide what you actually pay at that rate:

- What is the smallest unit you can rent? Some offers only rent whole 8-GPU servers, so the real hourly price is eight times the per-GPU rate.
- What is the billing granularity? Hourly billing rounds up. A 10-minute test on an hourly plan costs a full hour.

### How much do Model APIs cost?

For the latest pricing, you can visit our pricing page. Most models bill per output, such as per image, per megapixel or per second of video. MiniMax H3 Max is a good example, because duration and resolution both change the price. It bills per second of output video, and every clip includes synchronized audio. These are the published list rates, and what a 10-second clip costs:

| Endpoint | Resolution | Per second | 10-second clip |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H3 Max | 480p | $0.05 | $0.50 |
| H3 Max | 768p | $0.08 | $0.80 |
| H3 Max | 1080p | $0.16 | $1.60 |
| H3 Max Turbo | 480p | $0.025 | $0.25 |
| H3 Max Turbo | 768p | $0.04 | $0.40 |
| H3 Max Turbo | 1080p | $0.08 | $0.80 |

H3 Max's default request is a 5-second 768p clip, which costs $0.40. Price scales with both settings: a 15-second clip costs three times the 5-second default, and 1080p costs twice as much per second as 768p. H3 Max Turbo, the faster variant, costs half of H3 Max at every resolution.

Prices are also available programmatically from the pricing API, so you can show cost estimates in your own product.

...

### What do you pay for on Serverless?

Serverless billing is per second for the total time your runners are alive, by machine type:

- Billed: setup (loading your model), idle time (including `keep_alive`), running, draining and teardown.
- Not billed: waiting for a GPU (`PENDING`), pulling your image (`DOCKER_PULL`), and requests that fail with a 5xx error.

Warm capacity is the main cost lever. One H100 runner kept warm around the clock (`min_concurrency = 1`) for a 30-day month is 720 hours. That costs $3,240 at the $4.50/h list price, or $1,792.80 at the as-low-as rate of $2.49/h. Compare that to scaling to zero with a longer `keep_alive`, which only bills between bursts.
